subject: Dedicated pool sizing: burst runway, autoscale windows and throttle ops for Skyworks pilot
messages:
From: Elena Russo <elena@skyworks.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@skyworks.ai
Date: 2026-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & burst runway for Skyworks pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. We're trying to lock down capacity for the 90-day pilot. Attached is a short workbook with our expected traffic patterns (hourly requests and peak token rates) plus a sample night-batch job. Two asks from our side: 

1) Can Redwood outline the recommended dedicated pool sizing (GPU SKU mix + baseline slab) and an explicit burst runway (headroom in vGPU-equivalents) we should expect during the 90-day pilot?
2) We need the autoscaling/fallback behavior documented: if we exceed baseline and enter burst, what are the throttling policies, preemption behavior, and fallback model variants? Specifically we care about graceful degradation vs 429s and any queueing windows.

We have some procurement constraints (PO lead time), so if you can provide high-level guidance today that we can circulate to our finance/procurement team, that'd be great.

Thanks,
Elena Russo
Head of Platform Operations
Skyworks AI

Attachment: Skyworks_Workload_Profiles.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Russo <elena@skyworks.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & burst runway for Skyworks pilot

Elena —

Appreciate the workbook; it helped. Quick high-level answers while we run the sizing calc (Ben + Aditya are looping in sizing details below):

- Baseline recommendation: 4x A100-80GB equivalents (we'll propose mix with smaller GPUs if cost-sensitive) to meet sustained throughput in sheet 'baseline'.
- Burst runway: recommend 2.5x transient headroom (i.e., capacity to scale up to ~10 A100-80GB equiv) for short spikes; runway described in hours/days in the attached estimate.
- Autoscale behavior: our Dedicated autoscaler ramps in 60–180s for scheduled/observed increases (depends on cold start of new nodes). For immediate instant spikes we rely on ephemeral pre-warmed shoulder pool to absorb ~20% of baseline with <150ms added latency.
- Throttling & fallbacks: policy is graceful-first — prefix/KV cache hit routes to lower-cost variant; when queue exceeds N requests (configurable per-deal) we start returning 429s with Retry-After and concurrently spin extra shoulder capacity. Preemption applies to opportunistic instances only; reserved pool is not preempted without notice.

I'll attach a preliminary capacity estimate and a short runbook. Ben — any additions?

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-capacity-estimate-v1.xlsx (workbook, 44KB)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Elena Russo <elena@skyworks.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & burst runway for Skyworks pilot

Vanessa / Elena —

Couple of technical clarifications and a proposal for SLOs/mode behavior: 

- Sizing assumptions I used: 8 tokens/req avg for chat inference; peak qps from sheet -> ~600 qps sustained peak hour. That maps to the 4x A100 baseline Vanessa mentioned.
- Burst policy suggested: two-tier burst window:
   * Short burst (0–10min): shoulder pool + KV cache + eviction pressure; no model fallback unless latency > 1s.
   * Extended burst (10–120min): spin additional nodes up to 2.5x baseline; apply rate fairness across customers if aggregate pool saturated.
- Throttle behavior options (deal-configurable):
   1) Soft degrade: serve smaller-quantized model variant (recommended for chat UX) + inform via x-model-variant header.
   2) Queue + Retry: enqueue up to 5s, then 429/503 with Retry-After.
   3) Hard block: immediate 429 when headroom exhausted (for strict SLAs).

Recommendation for Skyworks pilot: default to Soft degrade + 5s queue before 429. We'll document exact queue size and fairness rules in the SLO appendix.

Notes on preemption: opportunistic GPUs (spot-equivalent) may be reclaimed by infra within minutes; we recommend keeping critical production request routes pinned to reserved slab. We can expose a per-route 'non-preemptible' flag in the tenant config.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcdEFgHIjkLmnoPqR/view (internal sizing doc)

From: Elena Russo <elena@skyworks.ai>

Cc: ops@skyworks.ai, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-26T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & burst runway for Skyworks pilot

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and SRE: 

- Procurement needs an explicit definition of "burst credits" and whether they are billed per-token or per-minute of extra-GPU usage. Can you provide an example cost calc for a 90-day pilot with the proposed runway?
- SRE wants the exact autoscale timeline so they can map our incident paging (we need to know when to open an on-call escalation if latency climbs). Can you give a deterministic timeline for the 60/180s ramps and specify which actions are synchronous vs asynchronous?

I've attached a draft PO with the pilot start date tentatively 2026-10-05. If we can get a short proc-friendly statement of work and a one-page capacity/runbook, procurement will fast-track the PO approval.

Elena Russo
Head of Platform Operations
Skyworks AI

Attachment: Skyworks_PO_0926.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Russo <elena@skyworks.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, ops@skyworks.ai
Date: 2026-09-27T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & burst runway for Skyworks pilot — next steps and SOW deliverables

Elena —

Great, we've pulled the items together. Action items and attachments below: 

1) Cost example: attached one-pager includes per-token and per-minute breakdown for baseline + burst credits for the 90-day window (we priced burst as a per-minute GPU-hour unit to simplify accounting; see table).
2) Autoscale timeline: deterministic steps in the runbook:
   - t0: sustained utilization spike detected by RT-metrics (5s window) -> pre-warmed shoulder absorbs up to 20% baseline immediately (synchronous route).
   - t0+60s: orchestrator requests new reserved nodes; warming kernels and model weights begin (asynchronous).
   - t0+120–180s: nodes join pool and traffic shifts; observed client latency should return to near-baseline.
   - If preemptible resources are reclaimed during spin-up, we fall back to soft-degrade variant until nodes fully join.
3) Throttle policy: default is Soft degrade + 5s queue before 429. We included optional stricter mode in appendix.
4) Deliverables: one-page SOW + 2-page runbook + pilot pricing example (attached). We will send signed SOW template for procurement by EOD.

Next steps: Ben/Aditya to finalize resource mix (A100 vs A10g split) and send a lockable quote. Laura will follow up on SLA addendum language for preemption guarantees.

I'll send the SOW and quote as separate items — ETA EOD tomorrow. Let me know if procurement needs different billing terms.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
